source.title: From Trajectories to Evidence: Auditable Experimental Records for Industrial Research Agents

assessments.primary_source_quality: Strong recent primary system paper with concrete industrial paper-to-target adaptations, artifact/provenance audits, claim qualification, frozen-memory diagnostics, applicability-controller evaluation, and candidate-level online outcomes. It is one-company evidence, recent/pre-peer-review in this pass, and no independent replication was identified.
assessments.quantitative_result: Across 30 adaptations, 26/30 had a later valid round outperform the first while 22/30 finished below an earlier best valid round, directly demonstrating non-monotonicity and the risk of equating latest state with best evidence. Bounded context-isolated generate/verify/repair raised proposal-gate acceptance 73.3%→100%, code completeness 92%→97%, and observability 67%→100%, while code alignment barely moved 50%→52%. Provenance audit reports 479/479 source-traceable spans, 107/107 source-supported mechanisms, 92.8% Method-section coverage, 87.4% Method-block coverage, and 34/34 referenced source artifacts matching archived SHA-256. Fourteen candidate claims were qualified into 8 Repairs, 1 Guard, and 5 Withheld. Applicability remained difficult: on 64 frozen target-record pairs the controller made 4 Apply decisions with only 1 reference match (25% affirmative precision), overall 67.2% accuracy versus 79.7% for always-Reject on the imbalanced set. In 8 paired frozen-memory diagnostics, even reference-applicable records included one harmful and one neutral application.
assessments.matched_baseline: Mixed. Strong descriptive within-system evidence for non-monotonic trajectories, qualification/provenance coverage and transfer failure. The bounded repair before/after metrics provide a useful treatment comparison but are not a randomized independent-controller experiment. Candidate-level online lifts lack a plain/no-memory parallel control and are explicitly not framework-level causal evidence.
assessments.ablation_or_causal_support: Moderate. The paper directly tests several verification/qualification components and exposes their limits, but the bundled candidate combines artifact verification, intervention grouping, record typing, provenance, applicability boundaries and best-valid-state preservation. No single ablation isolates the whole package versus simpler evidence retention.
assessments.reproducibility_or_artifacts: Strong provenance emphasis with archived source hashes and detailed record audits. This comparator relies on the worker's stated direct primary-PDF verification for exact table values and did not rerun the industrial system.
assessments.external_replication: None identified. Related research-agent integrity studies conceptually corroborate the need for artifact/provenance checks, but do not independently replicate this record-conversion workflow.
assessments.failure_evidence: Strong evidence that latest-round retention, same-model verification and automatic memory reuse are unsafe assumptions within this tested workflow. Particularly important: validated evidence and applicability are empirically separate bottlenecks.
scope_limits: Industrial recommendation paper-to-target adaptations inside one company.
Context isolation does not establish verifier independence; code alignment remained nearly unchanged.
Applicability controller was weak and imbalanced; valid evidence can transfer harmfully.
The +0.75% and +6.34% production candidate lifts cannot be attributed causally to the framework without no-framework controls.
A typed Repair/Guard/Withheld schema is one implementation, not demonstrated optimal ontology.

original_method_vs_o_adaptation.original_method_evidence: B+ for preserving qualified, provenance-bound evidence instead of chronological final state and for separating validity from applicability in the tested workflow; weaker for the controller and full bundled architecture.
original_method_vs_o_adaptation.o_specific_adaptation: C+/B- until O directly compares qualified-evidence records against simpler history/checkpoint retention on held-out downstream decisions and tests applicability gating with negative-transfer controls.

source.title: Distributed Denial of Science: How Indirect Data Poisoning of AI Systems Can Industrialize Scientific Fraud

assessments.primary_source_quality: Strong current primary preprint with an explicitly contained threat model, 450 runs, five topics, three frontier agent systems, a baseline attack rate, spontaneous detection measurement, and two mitigation interventions. It is not yet independently replicated in this pass.
assessments.quantitative_result: Across five socially salient topics, Claude Code/Claude Opus 4.7, Codex/GPT-5.5 and Gemini CLI/Gemini 3.1 Pro, indirect poisoned public datasets induced poisoned conclusions in 49.56% of 450 runs while poisoning was detected in only 6.0%. A scientist-persona intervention reduced but did not eliminate compromise, leaving 16.67% poisoned conclusions. A five-check retrieval-time provenance audit covering cited papers, social/context markers, statistical anomalies, related datasets and poisoning cautions reduced observed attack success to zero in the tested runs.
assessments.matched_baseline: Good: the paper explicitly compares ordinary agent behavior, scientist-persona prompting and the structured provenance-audit mitigation under the same attack class. The five-check bundle is not decomposed enough here to attribute benefit to individual checks.
assessments.ablation_or_causal_support: Moderately strong for the bundled provenance-audit mitigation in the tested attack environment. The zero observed post-mitigation successes provide a strong bounded result but not proof against arbitrary poisoning, compromised corroborating sources or adaptive attackers.
assessments.reproducibility_or_artifacts: The attack and audit procedure are specified in the primary source. This comparator did not independently recreate the 450-run campaign.
assessments.failure_evidence: Strong: honest autonomous research behavior can be subverted through retrieved data without prompt injection, malicious model access or fabricated papers; persona caution alone leaves substantial residual compromise.
scope_limits: Five topics and one specific indirect-poisoning construction with misleading metadata.
Zero observed audit failures is finite-sample evidence, not a universal security guarantee.
The audit assumes some independent provenance signals remain trustworthy.
The five-check bundle may impose retrieval/latency/false-rejection costs that require separate measurement for O or external research workers.

original_method_vs_o_adaptation.original_method_evidence: B+ for the five-check retrieval-time provenance audit against the tested indirect-data-poisoning attack.
original_method_vs_o_adaptation.o_specific_adaptation: C+/B- until O/research ingestion evaluates the audit on matched clean and corrupted data with false-positive, latency and coverage metrics; literature does not validate a universal provenance gate.

cross_source_synthesis: The record-conversion paper supports a high-value distinction: evidence validity, chronological recency and transfer applicability are separate variables. Its weak applicability controller is evidence against automatic reuse, not a reason to reject qualified evidence records.
The indirect-poisoning paper provides direct intervention evidence for retrieval-time provenance checks and also shows that a generic scientist persona is an incomplete integrity defense.

Both sources strengthen evidence hygiene but neither validates an O-specific implementation. O adaptations should be graded separately from the literature mechanisms and tested on held-out outcomes with false-positive/cost controls.
